fields.summary: Autonomous plan run on change set 01M6VY7G (Workflow dispatch). No owner took part: the planner raised two batches of questions and the arbiter answered each with a Decision worded (assumed, would have escalated). Facts from the code: the daemon starts every request's plan run with the built-in plan workflow (internal/api/request.go daemonStartPlan, planWorkflow in run.go), and every ready change set gets ship-change (defaultWorkflow in run.go); run start --new refuses any workflow other than plan; the change set records no request kind today; rhiza.toml is the root's machine-wide config (internal/rootcfg), shared by several projects and not committed in any repo. Settled by the arbiter in workflow-dispatch-shape: the change set serves milestone-25, the backlog milestone; the rules live in a committed repo file, .rhiza/dispatch.toml, not in rhiza.toml; rhiza request --workflow overrides only the ship pick and is recorded on the change set; a manual run start with no --workflow resolves the same way as the daemon. Settled in workflow-dispatch-rules-file: one table per trigger ([request] and [ready]) keyed by kind, with missing keys falling back to the built-in defaults and any other table or key an error; an unresolvable workflow name is a broken reference (rhiza check reports it, request --workflow refuses it, the daemon starts nothing and raises attention, never a silent fallback); a change set no request opened has kind feature; each run records what dispatch picked and why, shown in run ls and run status. Also found: rhiza change show fails on this change set because model.ShowFieldValue re-encodes a field with an @-reference using json.Marshal, which escapes '>' and fails the canonical check. That is outside this intent and goes to its own draft change set. Decision workflows-are-the-rules (PR #353) was not landed at plan time, so it is cited here but not linked.
fields.title: Workflow dispatch plan, autonomous run with the arbiter
